iterations.narrative:
The enrichment analysis identified **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** as the dominant pathway, with an FDR of 0.0 and a remarkable fold-enrichment of 603.3. Seven of the eleven input metabolites mapped to this pathway: choline (C00114), phosphoserine (C01005), sarcosine (C00213), adenosine monophosphate (C00020), S-adenosylmethionine (C00019), lipoic acid (C16241), and L-cystathionine (C02291). A cluster of SMPDB disease-coherence entries — including 3-Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase deficiency and non-ketotic hyperglycinemia — also achieved maximal significance, further pointing to a core disruption of one-carbon/amino-acid interconversion.

**Key driver compounds.** Phosphoserine anchors the upper end of the pathway as the direct entry point from glycolysis into serine biosynthesis. S-adenosylmethionine is the central methyl-group donor that connects one-carbon metabolism to phosphatidylcholine synthesis, neurotransmitter regulation, and trans-sulfuration. The KEGG reaction graph confirms a bidirectional path of three hops from phosphoserine through L-serine to sarcosine (C01005 → C00065 → C00037 → C00213), establishing that these two metabolites lie on the same linear segment. Similarly, choline is linked to SAM through a four-hop chain (C00114 → C00576 → C00719 → C00073 → C00019), consistent with choline's role as a methyl-group precursor feeding into the SAM cycle.

**Biological significance.** Glycine–serine–threonine metabolism sits at the intersection of amino-acid homeostasis, methylation capacity, and oxidative stress defence. Dysregulation of this hub — evident from coordinated changes in phosphoserine, sarcosine, SAM, and cystathionine — is known to impair one-carbon folate cycling, perturb transmethylation reactions, and compromise glutathione synthesis. The convergence on this pathway suggests the treatment condition imposes a metabolic stress that reprograms amino-acid catabolism and methyl-group availability, with downstream consequences for membrane-biology (via phosphatidylcholine) and redox buffering (via the trans-sulfuration arm producing cysteine).
